title: Taj Mahal
tagline: An ivory-white marble masterpiece of eternal love and UNESCO World Heritage Wonder

heroImage.alt: Taj Mahal in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India - Panoramic View with Iconic Reflecting Pool

overview.short: The Taj Mahal is an ivory-white marble mausoleum on the south bank of the Yamuna river in Agra, commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in 1631.
overview.description: Commissioned in 1631 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal, the Taj Mahal is recognized worldwide as the jewel of Muslim art in India and one of the universally admired masterpieces of the world's heritage. Set within a vast 17-hectare Mughal Charbagh garden complex with reflecting pools, red sandstone mosques, and intricate marble pietra dura inlay, it stands as an enduring symbol of eternal love.
overview.about: The Taj Mahal is universally celebrated as the greatest architectural achievement in the whole range of Indo-Islamic architecture. Its recognised architectonic beauty has a rhythmic combination of solids and voids, concave and convex and light and shadow; such as arches and domes further increases the aesthetic aspect. The relief carving in marble and inlay with precious and semi-precious stones make it a monument beyond compare.

topPlaces.name: Agra Fort
topPlaces.description: A monumental 16th-century Mughal fortress of red sandstone, featuring Jahangiri Mahal, Diwan-i-Am, Diwan-i-Khas, and breathtaking views of the Taj Mahal across the Yamuna.

image.alt: Agra Fort, Uttar Pradesh - Grand Red Sandstone Mughal Palaces and Fortifications

topPlaces.name: Mehtab Bagh
topPlaces.description: The historic charbagh Moonlight Garden situated perfectly across the Yamuna River, renowned as the ultimate sunset vantage point for reflection photos of the Taj Mahal.

image.alt: Mehtab Bagh, Agra - Sunset Reflection Garden View of the Taj Mahal across Yamuna

topPlaces.name: Tomb of I'timād-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
topPlaces.description: Often described as a 'jewel box' and the precursor to the Taj Mahal, this exquisite white marble mausoleum features delicate jali latticework and floral pietra dura inlay.

image.alt: Tomb of I'timad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj), Agra - Intricate White Marble Lattice Inlay

topPlaces.name: Fatehpur Sikri
topPlaces.description: The fortified 16th-century Mughal capital founded by Emperor Akbar, home to the colossal Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, and the serene Tomb of Salim Chishti.

image.alt: Fatehpur Sikri, Uttar Pradesh - Buland Darwaza and Imperial Mughal Red Sandstone Complex

topPlaces.name: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra
topPlaces.description: An architectural masterpiece combining red sandstone and white marble, set inside a vast 119-acre garden inhabited by peacocks and blackbucks.

image.alt: Akbar's Tomb, Sikandra - Grand Mughal Red Sandstone Gateway and Gardens

topPlaces.name: Jama Masjid, Agra
topPlaces.description: A monumental 17th-century congregational mosque built by Jahanara Begum, showcasing graceful inverted dome architecture and red sandstone courtyards.

image.alt: Jama Masjid Agra - Mughal Red Sandstone Architectural Facade

topPlaces.name: Chini Ka Rauza
topPlaces.description: The historic funerary monument of Mughal scholar-poet Afzal Khan Shirazi, famous for its rare Indo-Persian glazed polychrome enamel tiles.

image.alt: Chini Ka Rauza, Agra - Historic Indo-Persian Glazed Tile Architecture

topPlaces.name: Taj Nature Walk
topPlaces.description: A serene 180-acre nature reserve and forested trail located just 500 meters from the East Gate of Taj Mahal, offering elevated viewing towers and rich birdlife.

image.alt: Taj Nature Walk, Agra - Lush Green Walking Trails and Panoramic Viewing Points

itinerary.title: Day 1 — The Wonder of Taj Mahal & Mughal Agra Fort

items.note: Enter via East or West Gate at sunrise to witness the marble monument glow in soft pink and golden hues with minimal crowds.
Tour the red sandstone fortress, Jahangiri Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas, and view the Taj Mahal from Musamman Burj.
Cross to the north bank of the Yamuna River for sweeping sunset views and mirror reflections of the Taj Mahal.

itinerary.title: Day 2 — Heritage Jewels: Baby Taj, Sikandra & Fatehpur Sikri

items.note: Admire the delicate marble latticework and floral pietra dura inlay.
Visit the grand gateway and expansive garden pavilions where spotted deer roam freely.
Drive 36 km to explore the UNESCO World Heritage capital of Akbar, Buland Darwaza, and Salim Chishti Dargah.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit the Taj Mahal?
faq.a: The best time to visit is from October to March when the weather in Agra is pleasant (7–24°C). Sunrise is the best time of day for photography and avoiding crowds. Note that the Taj Mahal is closed on Fridays.

faq.q: Is Taj Mahal open on all days?
faq.a: The Taj Mahal is open from sunrise to sunset every day EXCEPT Friday, when it is closed for prayers.

faq.q: How to reach Taj Mahal from Delhi?
faq.a: The fastest way is via the Gatimaan Express or Vande Bharat train from Hazrat Nizamuddin Station to Agra Cantt (1 hr 40 mins), or via the 6-lane Yamuna Expressway by car (3–4 hrs).

faq.q: How many days are recommended for Agra and Taj Mahal?
faq.a: 2 days are ideal to explore the Taj Mahal at sunrise, Agra Fort, Mehtab Bagh, and the nearby UNESCO World Heritage city of Fatehpur Sikri.

faq.q: What is the entry ticket price for Taj Mahal?
faq.a: Indian citizens: ₹50 (+ ₹200 for main mausoleum dome); Foreign tourists: ₹1,100 (+ ₹200 for main mausoleum dome). Entry is free for children under 15.
